Un outil pour mesurer l'impact financier: A tool to measure the financial impact of AI on employment
Le Center for AI Safety (CAIS) met à dis: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) has released the "Wage Loss Dashboard" to quantify the financial repercussions of job cuts attributed to artificial intelligence. The tool includes a geographic map updated in September and a drop-down menu to analyze data nationwide or by state.
Le dispositif s'appuie sur les rapports: The system relies on monthly reports from Challenger, Gray and Christmas regarding layoff announcements, combined with Bureau of Labor Statistics data on average annual wages and demographic estimates from the U.S. Census Bureau.
À l'échelle du pays, le tableau de bord: Nationwide, the dashboard records just over 117,000 job cuts attributed to artificial intelligence this year, generating $8.5 billion in annual household wage losses. The average loss stands at $25 per person per year.
Toutefois, les chiffres varient fortemen: However, the figures vary significantly from state to state due to an uneven concentration of layoffs. California records more than 27,000 AI-related departures, representing an estimated loss of $56 per capita. Alaska, for its part, reports 138 job losses, or $14 per capita.
Le CAIS précise que ces estimations par: CAIS specifies that these state-by-state estimates are based on applying the national monthly share of job cuts to local announcements, followed by a division by the total population. The project excludes created jobs, productivity gains, and rehires, while emphasizing that companies self-report these job cuts without full transparency.
Le CAIS a lancé un tableau de bord pour: CAIS has launched a dashboard to quantify AI-related job losses.
